records.source: בְּ֭נִי תּוֹרָתִ֣י אַל־תִּשְׁכָּ֑ח וּ֝מִצְוֺתַ֗י יִצֹּ֥ר לִבֶּֽךָ׃
records.gloss: My son, my teaching do not forget, and my commandments let your heart keep,
pieces: My son, do not let my teaching slip from your memory; \q hold my commands close in your heart,

L.1: My son, my teaching do not forget, \q and my commandments let your heart keep,

R.1: My son, do not forget what I teach you. \q Remember my commands and obey them.

decisions.choice: teaching: the father's instruction
decisions.reason: The word (torah) is instruction, here the father's, as the mother's was in 1:8.

decisions.choice: keep: guard, hold on to
decisions.reason: The verb (natsar) means to guard, as a watchman does. The heart, the mind and will (2:2), is to keep watch over the commands.

records.heading: Keep my teaching

records.source: כִּ֤י אֹ֣רֶךְ יָ֭מִים וּשְׁנ֣וֹת חַיִּ֑ים וְ֝שָׁל֗וֹם יוֹסִ֥יפוּ לָֽךְ׃
records.gloss: for length of days and years of life and peace they will add to you.
pieces: for they will lengthen your days, add years to your life, \q and bring you peace.

L.2: for length of days and years of life \q and peace they will add to you.

R.2: If you do, you will live a long time, \q and your life will be full and peaceful.

decisions.choice: years of life and peace: a full and whole life
decisions.reason: "Years of life" may mean years really worth living, not only many years. Peace (shalom) is well-being of every kind, not only freedom from war.

records.source: חֶ֥סֶד וֶאֱמֶ֗ת אַֽל־יַעַ֫זְבֻ֥ךָ קָשְׁרֵ֥ם עַל־גַּרְגְּרוֹתֶ֑יךָ כָּ֝תְבֵ֗ם עַל־ל֥וּחַ לִבֶּֽךָ׃
records.gloss: Loyalty and faithfulness, let them not leave you; bind them on your neck; write them on [the] tablet of your heart,
pieces: Never let loyal love and faithfulness leave you: \q wear them like a necklace, \q and engrave them on your heart as on a tablet,

L.3: Loyal love and faithfulness, let them not leave you; \q bind them on your neck; \q write them on [the] tablet of your heart,

R.3: Always be loyal and kind, and keep your promises. \q Hold on to these things as if you wore them around your neck. \q Remember them as if they were written on your heart.

decisions.choice: loyal love and faithfulness: the son's own loyalty and reliability
alternatives: God's love and faithfulness toward the son
decisions.reason: The pair (hesed and emet) is often used of God (Exodus 34:6), but here they are qualities the son must keep, toward God and toward other people (14:22; 16:6; 20:28). Hesed is love that keeps faith; emet is being true and reliable.

decisions.choice: bind ... write: like the commands of Deuteronomy
decisions.reason: The picture recalls Deuteronomy 6:8–9, where God's words are to be bound on the hand and written on doorposts, and Jeremiah 31:33, where God writes his law on the heart. The tablet is a writing tablet (Isaiah 30:8).

decisions.choice: loyal love
decisions.reason: No one English word covers hesed. "Loyal love" keeps both its warmth and its faithfulness.

decisions.choice: as if you wore them ... as if they were written
decisions.reason: Readable makes the pictures into comparisons, so young readers do not take them literally.

records.source: וּמְצָא־חֵ֖ן וְשֵֽׂכֶל־ט֑וֹב בְּעֵינֵ֖י אֱלֹהִ֣ים וְאָדָֽם׃פ
records.gloss: and find favor and good insight in [the] eyes of God and humankind.
pieces: So you will find favor and be well thought of, \q both by God and by people.

L.4: and find favor and good regard \q in [the] eyes of God and humankind.

R.4: Then God and people will be pleased with you and think well of you.

decisions.choice: good regard: a good name, being well thought of
decisions.reason: The phrase (sekel tov) usually means good sense (13:15). Set beside "favor" and "in the eyes of", it means the good opinion that good sense wins.

decisions.choice: favor with God and people
decisions.reason: Samuel grew in favor with the LORD and with people (1 Samuel 2:26), and Luke says the same of the boy Jesus (Luke 2:52).

records.source: בְּטַ֣ח אֶל־יְ֭הוָה בְּכָל־לִבֶּ֑ךָ וְאֶל־בִּֽ֝ינָתְךָ֗ אַל־תִּשָּׁעֵֽן׃
records.gloss: Trust in YHWH with all your heart, and on your understanding do not lean.
pieces: Trust {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} with your whole heart, \q and do not rely on your own insight.

L.5: Trust in {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} with all your heart, \q and on your [own] understanding do not lean.

R.5: Trust {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} completely. \q Do not depend on what you think you know.

decisions.choice: trust: rely on with confidence
decisions.reason: The verb (batah) means to feel safe in someone and depend on them. It is the root of the "security" promised in 1:33 and 3:23.

decisions.choice: your own understanding: in contrast with the LORD
decisions.reason: Proverbs prizes understanding (verse 13). What it warns against is leaning on one's own insight instead of the LORD, as verse 7 says: "do not be wise in your own eyes".

decisions.choice: lean: put your weight on
decisions.reason: The verb (shaan) means to lean on something for support, like a staff (2 Kings 18:21).

records.heading: Trust God, not your own insight

records.source: בְּכָל־דְּרָכֶ֥יךָ דָעֵ֑הוּ וְ֝ה֗וּא יְיַשֵּׁ֥ר אֹֽרְחֹתֶֽיךָ׃
records.gloss: In all your ways know him, and he will make straight your paths.
pieces: Keep {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}} in mind in everything you do, \q and {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} will clear a straight road ahead of you.

L.6: In all your ways know {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}, \q and {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} will make your paths straight.

R.6: Remember {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} in everything you do, \q and {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} will lead you along the right road.

decisions.choice: know him: recognize and honor him in what you do
decisions.reason: To know (yada) God is to recognize him and live in relationship with him (Hosea 6:6; Jeremiah 22:16), not only to know about him.

decisions.choice: make straight: make level and clear, so that the way leads to its goal
decisions.reason: The verb (yashar) is used of leveling a road (Isaiah 40:3; 45:2). The LORD clears the way and brings the traveler where he should go (11:5; 15:21).

decisions.choice: Remember the LORD
decisions.reason: Readable names the LORD instead of "him", since the verse may be read on its own.

records.source: אַל־תְּהִ֣י חָכָ֣ם בְּעֵינֶ֑יךָ יְרָ֥א אֶת־יְ֝הוָ֗ה וְס֣וּר מֵרָֽע׃
records.gloss: Do not be wise in your eyes; fear YHWH and turn aside from evil.
pieces: Do not think of yourself as wise; \q fear {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} and keep away from evil.

L.7: Do not be wise in your [own] eyes; \q fear {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} and turn aside from evil.

R.7: Do not think you are wiser than you are. \q Honor {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} with awe, and stay away from evil.

decisions.choice: wise in your own eyes: wise in your own opinion
decisions.reason: The phrase is used of people who will not learn (26:12; Isaiah 5:21). The cure is the fear of the LORD, the beginning of wisdom (1:7).

decisions.choice: fear the LORD and turn from evil
decisions.reason: The pair describes Job (Job 1:1; 28:28) and recurs in 16:6.

records.source: רִ֭פְאוּת תְּהִ֣י לְשָׁרֶּ֑ךָ וְ֝שִׁקּ֗וּי לְעַצְמוֹתֶֽיךָ׃
records.gloss: Healing may it be to your navel and refreshment to your bones.
pieces: It will be medicine for your body \q and fresh strength for your bones.

L.8: Healing it will be to your navel, \q and refreshment to your bones.

R.8: Then your body will be healthy and strong.

decisions.choice: navel: the body
decisions.reason: The word (shor) is the navel or the cord at birth (Ezekiel 16:4), standing for the whole body. The ancient Greek translation read "body", from a Hebrew word that looks much the same.

decisions.choice: refreshment: moisture, life
decisions.reason: The word (shiqquy) means a drink. Healthy bones are pictured as moist and full of life, sick ones as dry (17:22; Job 21:24).

records.source: כַּבֵּ֣ד אֶת־יְ֭הוָה מֵהוֹנֶ֑ךָ וּ֝מֵרֵאשִׁ֗ית כָּל־תְּבוּאָתֶֽךָ׃
records.gloss: Honor YHWH from your wealth, and from [the] first of all your produce,
pieces: Honor {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} with what you own, \q with the first and best of everything your land produces;

L.9: Honor {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} from your wealth, \q and from [the] first of all your produce,

R.9: Honor {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} by giving {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}} the first and best part of everything you have.

decisions.choice: the first of all your produce: the firstfruits
decisions.reason: The law told Israel to bring the first of the harvest to the LORD (Exodus 23:19; Deuteronomy 26:2). The word (reshit) is the one translated "beginning" in 1:7: the first and best.

records.source: וְיִמָּלְא֣וּ אֲסָמֶ֣יךָ שָׂבָ֑ע וְ֝תִיר֗וֹשׁ יְקָבֶ֥יךָ יִפְרֹֽצוּ׃פ
records.gloss: and your barns will be filled [with] plenty, and [with] new wine your vats will burst.
pieces: then there will be more than enough to fill your barns, \q and new wine will burst out of your vats.

L.10: and your barns will be filled [with] plenty, \q and [with] new wine your vats will burst.

R.10: Then your barns will be full of grain, \q and you will have more wine than your vats can hold.

decisions.choice: a promise of how God's world works, not a guarantee of wealth
decisions.reason: Proverbs states how life generally goes under God's blessing (Deuteronomy 28:8). The same book knows that a little with the fear of the LORD is better than great treasure (15:16).

decisions.choice: new wine ... vats: the year's grape juice in the pressing vats
decisions.reason: The vat (yeqeb) is the trough below a winepress, where the juice runs (Joel 2:24).

records.source: מוּסַ֣ר יְ֭הוָה בְּנִ֣י אַל־תִּמְאָ֑ס וְאַל־תָּ֝קֹ֗ץ בְּתוֹכַחְתּֽוֹ׃
records.gloss: [The] discipline of YHWH, my son, do not reject, and do not loathe his rebuke,
pieces: My son, do not brush aside the discipline of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}, \q or grow weary of {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} correction,

L.11: The discipline of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}, my son, do not reject, \q and do not loathe {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} rebuke,

R.11: My son, when {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} disciplines you, do not refuse it. \q When {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} corrects you, do not get annoyed.

decisions.choice: discipline ... rebuke: correction, including hardship
decisions.reason: The LORD's discipline (musar) is the training a father gives (1:8). It may come as words or as hard things that correct (Deuteronomy 8:5).

decisions.choice: loathe: feel sick of, resent
decisions.reason: The verb (quts) means to feel disgust or dread at something (Genesis 27:46).

decisions.choice: quoted in Hebrews 12:5–6
decisions.reason: Hebrews quotes verses 11–12 from the ancient Greek translation to encourage believers who are suffering.

records.heading: {{divine_name:The LORD|Yahweh}}'s discipline and the worth of wisdom

records.source: כִּ֤י אֶ֥ת אֲשֶׁ֣ר יֶאֱהַ֣ב יְהוָ֣ה יוֹכִ֑יחַ וּ֝כְאָ֗ב אֶת־בֵּ֥ן יִרְצֶֽה׃
records.gloss: for [the one] whom YHWH loves he reproves, and like a father a son [in whom] he delights.
pieces: for {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} corrects the one {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} loves, \q as a father corrects the son who is his joy.

L.12: for whom {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} loves {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} reproves, \q even as a father the son [in whom] he delights.

R.12: {{divine_name:The LORD|Yahweh}} corrects the people {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} loves, \q the same way a father corrects a son he is pleased with.

decisions.choice: and like a father, as the Hebrew text reads
alternatives: and he punishes (the ancient Greek translation)
decisions.reason: With different vowels the same letters read "and he causes pain". The ancient Greek translation has "and he whips every son whom he receives", and Hebrews 12:6 quotes that form.

decisions.choice: whom the LORD loves he reproves: correction is a mark of love
decisions.reason: The point is the reason for verse 11: discipline shows that the LORD treats the son as his own (13:24; Deuteronomy 8:5).

records.source: אַשְׁרֵ֣י אָ֭דָם מָצָ֣א חָכְמָ֑ה וְ֝אָדָ֗ם יָפִ֥יק תְּבוּנָֽה׃
records.gloss: How blessed [is] a person [who] finds wisdom, and a person [who] obtains understanding,
pieces: How blessed is the person who has found wisdom, \q the one who has come by understanding,

L.13: How blessed [is the] person [who] has found wisdom, \q and [the] person [who] obtains understanding,

R.13: People who find wisdom are truly happy. \q So are people who gain understanding.

decisions.choice: how blessed: how well off, how happy
decisions.reason: The word (ashre) describes a person whose life is going well, as in Psalm 1:1. It is not the word for a blessing spoken by God (barak, as in verse 33). The same root closes this section in verse 18.

decisions.choice: how blessed
decisions.reason: "Happy" in English often means a passing mood. Literal and Balanced say "blessed"; Readable says "truly happy".

records.source: כִּ֤י ט֣וֹב סַ֭חְרָהּ מִסְּחַר־כָּ֑סֶף וּ֝מֵחָר֗וּץ תְּבוּאָתָֽהּ׃
records.gloss: for good [is] her profit more than profit of silver, and more than gold her gain.
pieces: for what she earns you is worth more than silver, \q and her return is better than gold.

L.14: for her profit [is] better than [the] profit of silver, \q and her gain [better] than gold.

R.14: Wisdom is worth more than silver and gold.

decisions.choice: profit ... gain: what trading brings in
decisions.reason: The words come from trade (sahar, merchandise; 31:18). Wisdom is pictured as a business that pays better than dealing in silver or gold.

decisions.choice: gold: fine gold
decisions.reason: The word (harus) is a poetic word for gold (8:10, 19; Psalm 68:14).

records.source: יְקָ֣רָה הִ֭יא מִפְּנִינִ֑ים וְכָל־חֲ֝פָצֶ֗יךָ לֹ֣א יִֽשְׁווּ־בָֽהּ׃
records.gloss: Precious [is] she more than corals, and all your delights do not compare with her.
pieces: She is worth more than red coral; \q nothing you long for comes close to her.

L.15: She [is] more precious than corals, \q and all your delights do not compare with her.

R.15: She is worth more than expensive jewels. \q Nothing you could want is as good as she is.

decisions.choice: corals: precious red stones
decisions.reason: The word (peninim) names something precious and reddish (Lamentations 4:7), most likely red coral. The exact stone is not certain.

decisions.choice: more than corals, as the scribes' reading has it
decisions.reason: The consonants written in the text (ketiv) and the reading the scribes marked (qere) spell this word differently; the meaning is the same.

records.source: אֹ֣רֶךְ יָ֭מִים בִּֽימִינָ֑הּ בִּ֝שְׂמֹאולָ֗הּ עֹ֣שֶׁר וְכָבֽוֹד׃
records.gloss: Length of days [is] in her right [hand]; in her left [are] wealth and honor.
pieces: She holds long life in her right hand, \q and wealth and honor in her left.

L.16: Length of days [is] in her right [hand]; \q in her left [are] wealth and honor.

R.16: Wisdom gives long life with one hand, \q and riches and honor with the other.

decisions.choice: right ... left: she offers gifts with both hands
decisions.reason: Wisdom is pictured as a woman holding out gifts. The promises are those of verse 2 and 8:18.

records.source: דְּרָכֶ֥יהָ דַרְכֵי־נֹ֑עַם וְֽכָל־נְתִ֖יבוֹתֶ֣יהָ שָׁלֽוֹם׃
records.gloss: Her ways [are] ways of pleasantness, and all her paths [are] peace.
pieces: Her ways are delightful, \q and every path she takes leads to peace.

L.17: Her ways [are] ways of pleasantness, \q and all her paths [are] peace.

R.17: Living wisely is pleasant, \q and it leads to peace.

decisions.choice: pleasantness ... peace: delight and well-being
decisions.reason: Pleasantness (noam) is what is lovely and delightful (Psalm 27:4); peace (shalom) is wholeness and well-being, as in verse 2.

records.source: עֵץ־חַיִּ֣ים הִ֭יא לַמַּחֲזִיקִ֣ים בָּ֑הּ וְֽתֹמְכֶ֥יהָ מְאֻשָּֽׁר׃פ
records.gloss: A tree of life [is] she to those taking hold of her, and [each one] holding her fast [is] called blessed.
pieces: To those who take hold of her she is a tree of life; \q whoever keeps a firm grip on her is called blessed.

L.18: She [is] a tree of life to those who take hold of her, \q and those who hold her fast [are] called blessed.

R.18: Wisdom is like a tree that gives life to people who hold on to it. \q People who hold on to it tightly are truly happy.

decisions.choice: a tree of life: as in the garden of Eden
decisions.reason: The tree of life stood in the garden (Genesis 2:9; 3:22–24). Wisdom gives what that tree gave: life. Proverbs uses the picture again in 11:30, 13:12 and 15:4, and Revelation 22:2 at the end of the Bible.

decisions.choice: those who hold her fast are called blessed
alternatives: each one who holds her fast is blessed
decisions.reason: The verb is singular with a plural subject, so it means "each of them". The word (meusshar) is from the same root as "how blessed" in verse 13, which closes the section.

records.source: יְֽהוָ֗ה בְּחָכְמָ֥ה יָֽסַד־אָ֑רֶץ כּוֹנֵ֥ן שָׁ֝מַ֗יִם בִּתְבוּנָֽה׃
records.gloss: YHWH by wisdom founded [the] earth; he established [the] heavens by understanding.
pieces: It was with wisdom that {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} set the earth on its foundations, \q and with understanding that {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} fixed the heavens in place;

L.19: {{divine_name:The LORD|Yahweh}} by wisdom founded [the] earth; \q {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} established [the] heavens by understanding;

R.19: {{divine_name:The LORD|Yahweh}} used wisdom to make the earth. \q He used understanding to put the sky in place.

decisions.choice: by wisdom: wisdom is how God made the world
decisions.reason: The wisdom the son is to find is the wisdom by which the LORD made all things (8:22–31; Psalm 104:24; Jeremiah 10:12). To live by it is to live with the grain of the world.

records.heading: Wisdom in creation and among neighbors

records.source: בְּ֭דַעְתּוֹ תְּהוֹמ֣וֹת נִבְקָ֑עוּ וּ֝שְׁחָקִ֗ים יִרְעֲפוּ־טָֽל׃
records.gloss: By his knowledge [the] deeps were split open, and [the] clouds drip dew.
pieces: by {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} knowledge the deep waters broke open, \q and the clouds let the dew fall.

L.20: by {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} knowledge [the] deeps were split open, \q and [the] clouds drip dew.

R.20: He knew how to make the springs break out of the ground, \q and how to make the clouds give dew.

decisions.choice: the deeps were split open: the springs broke out
alternatives: the waters were divided at creation
decisions.reason: The deeps (tehomot) are the waters below the earth. They broke out in the flood (Genesis 7:11), and they water the land in springs and rivers (Deuteronomy 8:7). Here the verse probably speaks of God giving water to the earth, as the second line does.

decisions.choice: clouds: the skies
decisions.reason: The word (shehaqim) means clouds or the skies (8:28; Job 36:28).

records.source: בְּ֭נִי אַל־יָלֻ֣זוּ מֵעֵינֶ֑יךָ נְצֹ֥ר תֻּ֝שִׁיָּ֗ה וּמְזִמָּֽה׃
records.gloss: My son, let them not depart from your eyes; keep sound wisdom and discretion,
pieces: My son, do not let these slip out of your sight; \q hold on to sound wisdom and foresight,

L.21: My son, let them not slip from your eyes; \q keep sound wisdom and discretion,

R.21: My son, keep good sense and wise planning in front of you. \q Hold on to them.

decisions.choice: them: sound wisdom and discretion, named in the second line
decisions.reason: The verb has no subject in the first line. The second line names it: sound wisdom and discretion. The verb (luz) is the one for "devious" in 2:15: turning aside.

decisions.choice: sound wisdom and discretion
decisions.reason: Sound wisdom (tushiyyah) is wisdom that works (2:7); discretion (mezimmah) is foresight (1:4; 2:11).

records.source: וְיִֽהְי֣וּ חַיִּ֣ים לְנַפְשֶׁ֑ךָ וְ֝חֵ֗ן לְגַרְגְּרֹתֶֽיךָ׃
records.gloss: and they will be life for your soul and grace for your neck.
pieces: and they will be life to you \q and a lovely ornament around your neck.

L.22: and they will be life for your soul \q and grace for your neck.

R.22: They will give you life, \q and they will make you attractive, like a beautiful necklace.

decisions.choice: grace for your neck: an ornament
decisions.reason: As in 1:9, wisdom is like an ornament worn around the neck, a mark of beauty and honor.

decisions.choice: soul: your whole self
decisions.reason: The word (nephesh) is the living person (2:10).

records.source: אָ֤ז תֵּלֵ֣ךְ לָבֶ֣טַח דַּרְכֶּ֑ךָ וְ֝רַגְלְךָ֗ לֹ֣א תִגּֽוֹף׃
records.gloss: Then you will walk in security your way, and your foot will not strike.
pieces: Then your road will be safe to walk, \q and your foot will not strike against anything.

L.23: Then you will walk your way in security, \q and your foot will not strike [against anything].

R.23: Then you will be safe wherever you go, \q and you will not trip and fall.

decisions.choice: your foot will not strike: you will not stumble
decisions.reason: The picture is of stubbing one's foot on a stone (Psalm 91:12). The safe road is the one the LORD makes straight (verse 6).

records.source: אִם־תִּשְׁכַּ֥ב לֹֽא־תִפְחָ֑ד וְ֝שָׁכַבְתָּ֗ וְֽעָרְבָ֥ה שְׁנָתֶֽךָ׃
records.gloss: If you lie down, you will not be afraid; and you will lie down, and your sleep will be sweet.
pieces: When you go to bed, you will have nothing to fear; \q you will lie down and sleep soundly.

L.24: If you lie down, you will not be afraid; \q you will lie down, and your sleep will be sweet.

R.24: When you go to bed, you will not be afraid. \q You will sleep well.

decisions.choice: if: when
decisions.reason: The word (im) here introduces a time, not a doubt: whenever you lie down.

records.source: אַל־תִּ֭ירָא מִפַּ֣חַד פִּתְאֹ֑ם וּמִשֹּׁאַ֥ת רְ֝שָׁעִ֗ים כִּ֣י תָבֹֽא׃
records.gloss: Do not be afraid of sudden dread, and of [the] devastation of wicked [people] when it comes,
pieces: You need not fear sudden terror, \q or the storm that falls on the wicked when it comes,

L.25: Do not be afraid of sudden dread, \q nor of [the] storm of [the] wicked when it comes,

R.25: Do not be afraid of sudden disaster \q or of the trouble that comes on evil people.

decisions.choice: the storm of the wicked: the ruin that falls on the wicked
decisions.reason: The phrase may mean the ruin that comes on the wicked, as in 1:27, where the same word (shoah) is used, or the ruin they bring on others. Verse 26 favors the first: the son need not fear being caught in it.

decisions.choice: dread: the thing dreaded
decisions.reason: The word (pahad) is the one in 1:26–27 and 1:33.

records.source: כִּֽי־יְ֭הוָה יִהְיֶ֣ה בְכִסְלֶ֑ךָ וְשָׁמַ֖ר רַגְלְךָ֣ מִלָּֽכֶד׃
records.gloss: for YHWH will be in your confidence, and he will keep your foot from capture.
pieces: for {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} will be the one you rely on, \q and {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} will keep your foot from the snare.

L.26: for {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} will be your confidence, \q and {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} will keep your foot from capture.

R.26: {{divine_name:The LORD|Yahweh}} will keep you safe. \q He will not let you be caught in a trap.

decisions.choice: your confidence: the one you rely on
decisions.reason: The word (kesel) can mean confidence (Job 8:14; Psalm 78:7) and also the loins or side. Some read "the LORD will be at your side".

decisions.choice: capture: being caught in a trap
decisions.reason: The word (leked) is used of an animal caught in a snare. It answers the net of 1:17.

records.source: אַל־תִּמְנַע־ט֥וֹב מִבְּעָלָ֑יו בִּהְי֨וֹת לְאֵ֖ל יָדְךָ֣ לַעֲשֽׂוֹת׃
records.gloss: Do not withhold good from its owners, when it is in [the] power of your hand to do [it].
pieces: When you have it in your power to do good to those who are owed it, \q do not hold it back.

L.27: Do not withhold good from its owners, \q when it is in [the] power of your hand to do [it].

R.27: When you are able to help someone, do it. \q Do not refuse to give people what they should have.

decisions.choice: its owners: those to whom it is due
decisions.reason: Literally "its owners", the people the good belongs to: wages owed (Leviticus 19:13), a debt, or help a neighbor has a right to expect.

decisions.choice: in the power of your hand: within your ability
decisions.reason: The phrase (el yad) means having it in one's power (Genesis 31:29; Micah 2:1).

records.source: אַל־תֹּ֘אמַ֤ר לְרֵֽעֲךָ֨׀לֵ֣ךְ וָ֭שׁוּב וּמָחָ֥ר אֶתֵּ֗ן וְיֵ֣שׁ אִתָּֽךְ׃
records.gloss: Do not say to your neighbor, Go and come back, and tomorrow I will give, when it is with you.
pieces: Do not tell your neighbor, \q "Go away and come back; I will give it to you tomorrow," \q when you have it with you now.

L.28: Do not say to your neighbor, \q "Go and come back, and tomorrow I will give [it]," \q when it is with you.

R.28: If your neighbor needs something you have, \q do not say, "Come back tomorrow, and I will give it to you then."

decisions.choice: to your neighbor, as the scribes' reading has it
decisions.reason: The written consonants (ketiv) can be read as plural, "your neighbors"; the reading the scribes marked (qere) is singular. The meaning is the same.

decisions.choice: neighbor: anyone you live among
decisions.reason: The neighbor (rea) is the person beside you, as in Leviticus 19:18.

records.source: אַל־תַּחֲרֹ֣שׁ עַל־רֵעֲךָ֣ רָעָ֑ה וְהֽוּא־יוֹשֵׁ֖ב לָבֶ֣טַח אִתָּֽךְ׃
records.gloss: Do not devise against your neighbor harm, while he dwells in security with you.
pieces: Do not plot harm against your neighbor, \q who lives beside you and trusts you.

L.29: Do not devise harm against your neighbor, \q while {{gender:they are|he is}} dwelling in security beside you.

R.29: Do not plan to hurt your neighbor, \q who lives next to you and trusts you.

decisions.choice: devise: plot, work out
decisions.reason: The verb (harash) is to plow or engrave, and so to work out a plan (6:14; 12:20).

decisions.choice: dwelling in security: living without suspicion
decisions.reason: The neighbor lives beside you trusting you. To plot against such a person is a betrayal.

records.source: אַל־תָּרִ֣יב עִם־אָדָ֣ם חִנָּ֑ם אִם־לֹ֖א גְמָלְךָ֣ רָעָֽה׃
records.gloss: Do not contend with a person without cause, if he has not dealt to you harm.
pieces: Do not pick a fight for no reason \q with someone who has done you no wrong.

L.30: Do not contend with anyone without cause, \q if {{gender:they have|he has}} not done you harm.

R.30: Do not argue with someone for no reason \q when that person has not hurt you.

decisions.choice: contend, as the scribes' reading has it
decisions.reason: The written consonants (ketiv) and the scribes' reading (qere) give two spellings of the same verb.

decisions.choice: contend: quarrel, or bring a case at law
decisions.reason: The verb (rib) covers both a quarrel and a lawsuit (25:8–9). Either way the son must not start one without cause.

records.source: אַל־תְּ֭קַנֵּא בְּאִ֣ישׁ חָמָ֑ס וְאַל־תִּ֝בְחַ֗ר בְּכָל־דְּרָכָֽיו׃
records.gloss: Do not be jealous of a man of violence, and do not choose any of his ways,
pieces: Do not be jealous of the violent, \q and do not take up any of their ways,

L.31: Do not envy {{gender:a person|a man}} of violence, \q and do not choose any of {{gender:their|his}} ways,

R.31: Do not be jealous of people who hurt others to get what they want. \q Do not live the way they do.

decisions.choice: violence: wrongdoing by force
decisions.reason: The word (hamas) is violence and injustice of every kind, the kind the gang of 1:10–19 practiced (Genesis 6:11).

decisions.choice: be jealous: envy their success
decisions.reason: The danger is envying the violent because they seem to prosper (23:17; 24:1, 19; Psalm 37:1).

records.source: כִּ֤י תוֹעֲבַ֣ת יְהוָ֣ה נָל֑וֹז וְֽאֶת־יְשָׁרִ֥ים סוֹדֽוֹ׃
records.gloss: for an abomination of YHWH [is the] crooked, but with [the] upright [is] his intimacy.
pieces: for the devious are hateful to {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}, \q but the upright are {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} close friends.

L.32: for the devious [is] an abomination to {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}, \q but with [the] upright [is] {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} intimate counsel.

R.32: {{divine_name:The LORD|Yahweh}} hates it when people are dishonest. \q But {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} is a close friend to people who do what is right.

decisions.choice: abomination: something detestable
decisions.reason: The word (toevah) names what God finds detestable (6:16; 11:1, 20). In Proverbs it is used mostly of moral wrongs.

decisions.choice: intimate counsel: confidential friendship
decisions.reason: The word (sod) is a circle of close friends and the secrets shared there (Psalm 25:14; Amos 3:7).

records.source: מְאֵרַ֣ת יְ֭הוָה בְּבֵ֣ית רָשָׁ֑ע וּנְוֵ֖ה צַדִּיקִ֣ים יְבָרֵֽךְ׃
records.gloss: [The] curse of YHWH [is] on [the] house of [the] wicked, but [the] dwelling of righteous [people] he blesses.
pieces: The house of the wicked lies under the curse of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}, \q but the home where the righteous live receives {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} blessing.

L.33: The curse of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} [is] on [the] house of [the] wicked, \q but [the] dwelling of [the] righteous {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} blesses.

R.33: {{divine_name:The LORD|Yahweh}} puts a curse on the homes of evil people, \q but {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} blesses the homes of good people.

decisions.choice: dwelling: a home, even a humble one
decisions.reason: The word (naweh) can mean a pasture or shepherd's camp (Jeremiah 33:12), and so a modest home, set against the wicked man's house.

records.source: אִם־לַלֵּצִ֥ים הֽוּא־יָלִ֑יץ וְ֝לַעֲנָוִ֗ים יִתֶּן־חֵֽן׃
records.gloss: Though to mockers he mocks, to humble [people] he gives grace.
pieces: Mockers {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} meets with mockery, \q but to the humble {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} gives grace.

L.34: Though to mockers {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} mocks, \q yet to [the] humble {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} gives grace.

R.34: {{divine_name:The LORD|Yahweh}} laughs at people who laugh at others, \q but {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} is kind to humble people.

decisions.choice: the humble, as the scribes' reading has it
decisions.reason: The written consonants (ketiv) read "the poor" or "the afflicted"; the reading the scribes marked (qere) is "the humble". The two words are close in Hebrew, and the poor and the humble are often the same people in Scripture.

decisions.choice: quoted in James 4:6 and 1 Peter 5:5
decisions.reason: Both letters quote this verse from the ancient Greek translation: "God opposes the proud but gives grace to the humble".

decisions.choice: he: the LORD of verse 33
decisions.reason: The subject carries over from verse 33. As in 1:26, the mocker is answered in his own terms.

decisions.choice: The LORD
decisions.reason: Readable names the LORD, since the verse is often read on its own.

records.source: כָּ֭בוֹד חֲכָמִ֣ים יִנְחָ֑לוּ וּ֝כְסִילִ֗ים מֵרִ֥ים קָלֽוֹן׃פ
records.gloss: Honor wise [people] will inherit, but fools [are] lifting up shame.
pieces: Honor is what the wise inherit, \q but fools are held up to disgrace.

L.35: [The] wise will inherit honor, \q but fools [are] lifting up shame.

R.35: Wise people will be honored, \q but fools will be put to shame.

decisions.choice: fools are lifting up shame: disgrace is what they get
decisions.reason: The verb is singular beside the plural "fools", and the line is hard. Most likely it means that what fools carry off is disgrace, set against the honor the wise inherit.
